body.hook: China's currency is called 人民币 Rénmínbì, "the people's money." In everyday speech people say 块 kuài instead of 元 yuán, and 毛 máo for ten cents. Knowing both helps you read prices and hear them.

study.title: 人民币
study.question: How do I read and say prices in Chinese money?
study.passage:
Money guide (written for this lesson):
1 元 (yuán) = 10 角 (jiǎo) = 100 分 (fēn).
Spoken: 块 kuài for 元, 毛 máo for 角.
Prices: ¥5.00 五块 wǔ kuài; ¥2.00 两块 liǎng kuài; ¥3.50 三块五 (毛) sān kuài wǔ (máo); ¥12.80 十二块八 shí'èr kuài bā; ¥0.50 五毛 wǔ máo; ¥99 九十九块.
The last unit is often dropped: 三块五 = 3.50.
Written price tags use ¥ and decimals: ¥25.00 or 25元.
Exchange: exchange rates change daily; your teacher will give a current approximate rate between Canadian dollars (加元) and yuan. Use it for estimates only.
Today, many people in China pay with phone apps (scanning QR codes), but cash is still accepted and used.
Activity: price-tag reading race: teams read price tags aloud in spoken form (块/毛); then convert three prices to Canadian dollars using the teacher's rate.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; exchange rates vary and should be checked when used.

body.hook: 多少钱? Duōshao qián? "How much?" is the essential shopping question. At markets in China, polite bargaining is sometimes expected, so you'll also learn how to say "too expensive!"

study.title: 多少钱?
study.question: How do I ask prices and bargain politely?
study.passage:
Shopping phrases (written for this lesson):
Asking: 这个多少钱? Zhège duōshao qián? (How much is this?) 这件衣服多少钱? (How much is this piece of clothing?) 一本书多少钱?
Answers: 五十块。
Reacting: 太贵了! (Too expensive!) 便宜一点, 可以吗? Piányi yìdiǎn, kěyǐ ma? (A bit cheaper, OK?)
Agreeing: 好, 我买了。(OK, I'll buy it.) / 不要了, 谢谢。(I don't want it, thanks.)
Measure words: 件 jiàn (clothes: 一件T恤), 本 běn (books: 两本书), 双 shuāng (pairs: 一双鞋 shoes), 个 gè (general: 一个包 bag).
买 mǎi (buy, third tone) vs 卖 mài (sell, fourth tone): the tone changes the meaning!
Culture: in many outdoor markets and small stalls, friendly bargaining is common; in department stores and supermarkets, prices are fixed. Always stay polite and smile.
Activity: partners practise with price cards: one asks, the other answers, then they bargain politely.

body.hook: Welcome to the class 市场 shìchǎng (market)! Today some of you are sellers and some are shoppers, and everything happens in Mandarin, from greeting to bargaining to paying.

study.title: 中文市场
study.question: How do I shop and sell in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Market model (written for this lesson):
卖家 (seller): 欢迎光临! 你要什么?
买家 (buyer): 你好! 这件T恤多少钱?
卖家: 六十块。
买家: 太贵了! 五十块, 可以吗?
卖家: 好, 可以。还要别的吗?
买家: 我还要两本书。
卖家: 两本书二十块。一共七十块。
买家: 给你一百块。
卖家: 找你三十块。谢谢, 下次见!
Setup: sellers run stalls (clothes 衣服, books 书, fruit 水果, snacks 零食) with price tags in ¥. Buyers get ¥200 in play money and a shopping list.
Rules: everything in Mandarin; use measure words; bargain politely at least once; sellers calculate totals and change.
Afterward: buyers record what they bought and spent; sellers record what they sold. Reflection: which phrases did you use most?
